page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadsv7 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, offering 945 GB of capacity with Premium Storage capability, while no GPUs are included.

In performance benchmarks, the E16-4ads_v7 exhibits strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance is more constrained due to the 4-vCPU limit. Multi-core stress-ng performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average category, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, placing in the bottom quarter of tested servers. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET operations, consistently perform within the average range.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this server is defined by its high resource density, offering a massive memory footprint relative to its compute allocation. This makes it a highly specialized option where memory capacity is prioritized over parallel processing power. The primary tradeoff is the limited multi-threaded compute scaling, as evidenced by the lower multi-threaded benchmark tiers. This configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling, such as in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and lightweight data processing tasks.
